text: Somewhere behind you or ahead of you, another set of prints is going the same direction for a while. You did not agree on it and neither of you is following. Gebo is that overlap — two goings that share the ground without owing each other the route. Where the tracks part, neither one turns to check.

While you have been walking, something has been getting on with itself in the ground you left behind. Berkana is that working underneath — it did not need you there and it did not wait for you to be ready. Whatever you find when you turn back will be further along than the day you set out.

There is a stretch where the going stops costing. Not because the way got easier, but because you are among people who know your name and the walking does not have to be explained. It lasts as long as it lasts. The way runs on past it either way.
